next_question: Does the orthogonality boundary lie at ~25% Gaussian overlap (where RC-25%-TOST fails at n=480 with r=0.080) rather than 50% — and does n>=800 at 25% overlap resolve this failure under Bonferroni correction, establishing a stable usable envelope of 0-50%?
why_next: This experiment resolved the parent's 50% orthogonality failure as a Type I sampling artifact: null-control 50% n=480 PASSES (r=-0.044, contradicting parent r=0.080), and primary 50% n=1000 PASSES decisively (r=-0.003, CI 0.059). However, a NEW failure emerged at 25% overlap (r=0.080, CI 0.168 at n=480) with identical magnitude to the parent's 50% failure, demonstrating stochastic Type I wander (9.4% per-test, 25.6% family-wise). The non-monotonic orthogonality pattern (strongest at 25%, not 50%) suggests the independence assumption boundary may be lower than hypothesized. The NC-0% FP=0.025 failure is threshold misspecification (theoretical tail 0.0179 > 0.01 control), not measurement failure. The highest-information question is whether n>=800 at 25% resolves the 25% TOST failure, which would either establish 0-50% usable envelope or confirm the 0-25% ceiling as real.
